text: Agile methodology is a popular approach to project management, especially in software development. Instead of planning everything upfront, work is divided into short cycles called sprints, which usually last two to four weeks. Every day, the team holds a quick standup meeting to discuss progress, plans for the day, and any problems. Before each sprint, they select tasks from a backlog, which is a list of features and improvements to be made. These tasks are often described as user stories, explaining a feature from the user's perspective. This iterative development allows the team to adapt quickly to feedback and changes.
